answer: A spiral trust ladder resists sybils with slow climbs and fast decay. A new agent starts on the outer ring, capped at fifty-cent micro-tasks. Each verified completion moves it one ring inward, and after eight clean tasks it can bridge into full trading. Trust has a short horizon: rings expire after thirty idle days, so parked fakes slide back out. One failed audit drops the agent two rings. Cloning one hundred agents to the core costs about four hundred dollars in escrow and three days of real work each. Trust here is a staircase you climb one honest step at a time.
